slides.text: Cobra writes the help of every command for you. What you set on a command (a summary, a description, examples, flags) is what people read when they ask for help.

Two texts come out of it. The **help** is the full screen shown by `--help`. The **usage** is its short part: the usage line, the examples and the flags.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
help  = description
      + usage
usage = usage line
      + examples
      + flags

slides.text:
Every field you set lands in a fixed place of the help screen. Cobra only fills the layout in.

The snippet is the shape of that text, with each part named.
slides.code:
<description>

Usage:
  <usage line> [flags]

Examples:
  <examples>

Flags:
  <flags and their text>

slides.text: The flags come with the text you gave them, and with their default when it is not empty. The commands of a parent are listed by their short summary.

slides.text: Help is on without any code: `--help` and `-h` on every command, and a `help` command on a command with subcommands.
From the code you can print the help or only the usage, or take the usage as a string to build your own message. A command can also carry a version, which gets its own flag.

`--version` prints the command name and the version, like `greet version 1.2.0`. `SetVersionTemplate` replaces that text with a template of your own, as in this pseudo code, filled from the command: `{{.Version}}` becomes the version.

slides.text: Some things should not show in the help: a command for you only, a flag nobody should use, an old name on its way out. Cobra can hide or retire them without deleting code.

When the built-in text is not what you want, give Cobra your own function for the help, or keep the layout and change a template.

A template is text with placeholders in double braces, filled from the command. The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
template: Usage: {{ usage line }}
result:   Usage: greet [flags]
